reason: This case is the inverse defect shape: the buggy tree is the one that CONTAINS a null guard (`if (cache != null && key != null)`) and the fix REMOVES it because the `key != null` check silently defeats the cache, whereas the accumulated rule fires only on UNGUARDED dereferences that can NPE — a single generalized rule cannot simultaneously require the guard (for case 2's buggy tree) and forbid it (for case 4's fixed tree), so it can't fire on every covered buggy tree while staying silent on every covered fixed tree.
